In this activity, we will look at the span of sets of vectors in $\real^3$.

Suppose $\vvec=\threevec{1}{2}{1}$. Give a geometric description of $\laspan{\vvec}$ and a rough sketch of $\vvec$ and its span in [fig-3d-span-1].

A three-dimensional coordinate system for sketching $\vvec$ and its span.

Now consider the two vectors $$ \evec_1 = \threevec{1}{0}{0},~~~ \evec_2 = \threevec{0}{1}{0} $$ . Sketch the vectors below. Then give a geometric description of $\laspan{\evec_1,\evec_2}$ and a rough sketch of the span in [fig-3d-span-2].

A coordinate system for sketching $\evec_1$, $\evec_2$, and $\laspan{\evec_1,\evec_2}$.

Let's now look at this situation algebraically by writing write $\bvec = \threevec{b_1}{b_2}{b_3}$. Determine the conditions on $b_1$, $b_2$, and $b_3$ so that $\bvec$ is in $\laspan{\evec_1,\evec_2}$ by considering the linear system $$ \left[\begin{array}{rr} \evec_1 \amp \evec_2 \\ \end{array}\right] ~\xvec = \bvec $$ or $$ \left[\begin{array}{rr} 1 \amp 0 \\ 0 \amp 1 \\ 0 \amp 0 \\ \end{array}\right] \xvec = \threevec{b_1}{b_2}{b_3} $$ . Explain how this relates to your sketch of $\laspan{\evec_1,\evec_2}$.

Consider the vectors $$ \vvec_1 = \threevec{1}{1}{-1},~~ \vvec_2 = \threevec{0}{2}{1}. $$

Is the vector $\bvec=\threevec{1}{-2}{4}$ in $\laspan{\vvec_1,\vvec_2}$?

Is the vector $\bvec=\threevec{-2}{0}{3}$ in $\laspan{\vvec_1,\vvec_2}$?

Give a geometric description of $\laspan{\vvec_1,\vvec_2}$.

Consider the vectors $$ \vvec_1 = \threevec{1}{1}{-1}, \vvec_2 = \threevec{0}{2}{1}, \vvec_3 = \threevec{1}{-2}{4} $$ . Form the matrix $\left[\begin{array}{rrrr} \vvec_1 \amp \vvec_2 \amp \vvec_3 \end{array}\right]$ and find its reduced row echelon form.

What does this tell you about $\laspan{\vvec_1,\vvec_2,\vvec_3}$?

If the span of a set of vectors $\vvec_1,\vvec_2,\ldots,\vvec_n$ is $\real^3$, what can you say about the pivot positions of the matrix $\left[\begin{array}{rrrr} \vvec_1\amp\vvec_2\amp\ldots\amp\vvec_n \end{array}\right]$?

What is the smallest number of vectors such that $\laspan{\vvec_1,\vvec_2,\ldots,\vvec_n} = \real^3$?
